title: Colorado home sales fell nearly 19% in October as prices held
h1: Colorado home sales dropped nearly 19% in October while the median price barely moved, Realtors report
description: Colorado recorded 6,079 home sales in October 2026, down 18.6% from a year earlier, while the statewide median price slipped 0.9% to $545,000, Realtors data show.
standfirst: Far fewer Colorado homes changed hands in October than a year ago, but prices have hardly budged. Sellers are leaning on concessions and price cuts instead, and mortgage rates near 7.5% are keeping buyers on the sidelines.
keywords: Colorado home sales October 2026, Colorado housing market, Denver median home price, Colorado Association of Realtors, seller concessions Denver, mortgage rates 7.5 percent
takeaways: Colorado had 6,079 closed home sales in October 2026, down 18.6% from October 2025, and pending contracts fell 17.2%, according to the Colorado Association of Realtors.
The statewide median price was $545,000, down 0.9%. In the seven-county Denver metro area, sales fell 20.6% and the median was $571,000.
The 30-year fixed mortgage rate stood at 7.5%, up from 6.4% a year earlier, The Colorado Sun reported, citing Mortgage News Daily.
body: Colorado's housing market slowed sharply in October. The state recorded 6,079 closed home sales, down 18.6% from October 2025, the Colorado Association of Realtors said in its monthly market report, released November 12. Pending contracts, a sign of future closings, fell 17.2%.

Prices did not follow. The statewide median sale price was $545,000, down 0.9% from a year earlier. Single-family homes had a median of $575,000, down 0.7%, and condos and townhomes came in at $415,000, up 0.2%. New listings fell 8.9% and 33,455 homes were for sale at the end of the month, 2.4% fewer than a year ago.
What is happening in the Denver area?
The seven-county Denver metro area had 3,473 closed sales, down 20.6%, with a median price of $571,000, down 0.8%. The median for a single-family home was $619,000.

The sale price does not tell the whole story. About 64% of Denver County sales in October included a seller concession, up from 55% two years ago, The Colorado Sun reported, and the Realtors report said roughly half of metro sales involved a price reduction. We covered the rise in Denver price cuts in September.

Agents point to borrowing costs. The 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.5% as of Friday, compared with 6.4% a year earlier, the Sun reported, citing Mortgage News Daily. The Realtors group said its statewide measure of affordability fell 8.4% from a year ago.
The Sun also reported that Denver's average rent fell 2.4% from a year earlier in October, which gives would-be buyers less reason to rush.

The association publishes its figures monthly. In southwest Colorado, a Pagosa Springs agent quoted in the report said two major floods and damage to U.S. 160 are hurting year-end sales there. The report draws on listing-service data and leaves out most new construction and homes sold directly by owners.
